evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field puts the beginning at 06:02 Pacific on 4 June 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End field gives 07:45 Pacific, matching the stated 1 hour 43 minute duration. regions: Mini Incident Report, Regions/Zones lists three us-east1 zones; workaround says zone us-east1-a remained usable.
notes: Published date is the Mini Incident Report posting (6 Jun 2023 07:26 PDT). Scope regional: three zones of one region affected, us-east1-a stated as a working alternative. Status update says resolved for all users at 08:14 PDT; Incident End 07:45 PDT used as end of impact. Services: Compute Engine, Kubernetes Engine, Dataflow, Cloud SQL. PDT = UTC-7.

evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field sets the beginning at 12:47 Pacific on 7 May 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End and the rollback of the Console change both fall at 17:06 Pacific. regions: Mini Incident Report gives Global as the location; page header lists 37 previously affected regions.
notes: Mini Incident Report posted 8 May 2023 23:17 PDT, which is 9 May 2023 in UTC; the page shows 8 May. Scope global because Regions/Zones reads Global; regions are the 37 locations the header lists as previously affected. Rollback mitigation at the same minute as Incident End. Status update says resolved at 17:19 PDT. Only Cloud SQL named as impaired (root cause was a Cloud Console UI change). PDT = UTC-7.

evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field gives 06:05 Pacific on 6 May 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End field gives 10:35 Pacific, consistent with a 4 hour 30 minute outage. regions: Mini Incident Report lists zone europe-west9-c and region europe-west9, with impacts grouped under both.
notes: Published date is the Mini Incident Report posting (15 May 2023 12:05 PDT). Coded regional, not zonal: Regions/Zones names europe-west9 as well as europe-west9-c, and Customer Impact lists region-level impacts (Interconnect, Pub/Sub, KMS, GCS, Cloud SQL, Networking, Dataflow); status of other europe-west9 zones not stated. Early status updates gave a 06:40 PDT start; the report's 06:05 PDT used. PDT = UTC-7.

evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field gives 12:02 Pacific on 5 May 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End 12:58 Pacific, when faulty routers were pulled and traffic rerouted. regions: Page header names Madrid (europe-southwest1); report describes edge peering routers in Madrid affecting Spain and Morocco users.
notes: Published date is the Mini Incident Report posting (10 May 2023 14:23 PDT). Regions/Zones in the report reads Multi Region Europe without naming further regions; the only named location is europe-southwest1, so coded regional. Impact was at the network edge for ISPs peering in Madrid; all GCP services were unreachable for those users but not named individually. Services counted: Gmail (Workspace) and Google Cloud Networking. Mitigation and resolution also at 12:58 PDT. PDT = UTC-7.

evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field gives 08:47 Pacific on 3 May 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End field gives 03:10 Pacific on 4 May, matching the 18 hour 23 minute duration. regions: Mini Incident Report names two Asian regions, Singapore and Taiwan, for the intermittent packet loss.

evidence: start: Incident Report Summary says BigQuery connection errors began at 14:18 Pacific on 28 April 2023. end: Incident Report impact section and remediation put the end, after killing the faulty job, at 13:10 Pacific on 29 April. regions: Report places impact only in the US multi-region and US regions, naming no region codes.
notes: Published date is the full Incident Report (10 May 2023 15:27 PDT); a Mini Incident Report was posted 2 May 2023. Start times conflict within the page: Incident Report Summary 14:18 PDT, Detailed Description of Impact 14:24 PDT, Mini Incident Report and header 18:00 PDT; the earliest stated, 14:18 PDT, is used. Stated 19 hour 10 minute duration matches only the 18:00 start. Status update says resolved at 12:00 PDT on 29 Apr, against 13:10 PDT in both reports. Location is the BigQuery US multi-region (us), which is not a region: no code added, scope unclear. PDT = UTC-7.

evidence: start: Mini Incident Report, Incident Start field gives 01:58 Pacific on 26 April 2023. end: Mini Incident Report, Incident End 04:56 Pacific, after the rollback and configuration propagation finished. regions: Mini Incident Report gives Global; description says HTTPS load balancer updates failed worldwide; header lists 35 regions.
notes: Published date is the Mini Incident Report posting (27 Apr 2023 10:09 PDT). Regions are the 35 locations the header lists as previously affected. evidence: start: Incident Report timeline, at 18:30 Pacific on 25 April Google began taking zone-a VMs and disks offline. end: Incident Report timeline, by 19:00 Pacific on 26 April Compute recovered in all zones and the region was largely operational. regions: Page lists Paris (europe-west9) and Global; report describes regional loss plus global Console and API failures.
notes: Published date is the full Incident Report (23 Jun 2023 09:12 PDT). Header incident start 16:46 PDT on 25 Apr is when the water leak began, not stated customer impact; first stated impact is the GCE/PD shutdown from 18:30 PDT. Regional impact began 23:04 PDT (timeline) or 23:29 PDT (narrative); global Console/API impact from 23:04 PDT (status updates: 23:15 PDT) to 03:38 PDT on 26 Apr, global not a region so region_starts left empty. End is the 19:00 PDT region recovery; header end is 20:00 PDT, and 58% of europe-west9-a VMs stayed down longer (cluster later decommissioned, data recovered). Zones b and c included because updates state services recovered in them. Scope global because the location Global is listed. services_n counts the 38 products in the header list (no enumerated list in the report). PDT = UTC-7.
